entries.group: T05-FIRST-ATTRIBUTION: _known's guard `and old not in known` keeps the release attribution of a migrated/kept approval; swapping it to `or` fabricates a cross-release provenance and breaks the documented 'first attribution' invariant.
entries.grounds: mutant_view: `if old is not None and old not in known:` -> `if old is not None or old not in known:` (bundle_cli.py:168, inside the per-release loop that sets `known[old], origin[old] = s.id, name`). The function docstring (L160-162) states 'an id two releases compile keeps the first attribution', and `origin` is the release a kept/migrated contract is attributed to. Two reachable behaviour changes the guard exists to prevent: (a) when a release's probe is byte-identical to the current active probe, `_earlier(s, release).id == s.id`, so `old` is already in `known` as a current id — the original keeps origin[old]='current', the mutant (`or`, since `old is not None` is True) OVERWRITES it to the release name; (b) with two RELEASES entries both compiling a spec to the same `old` id, the original keeps the first release (the `and old not in known` guard), the mutant overwrites with the later one. MEASURED (demo_known.py, run under tests.v2 import): a release R whose probes equal catalog.active() plus migrate(era_bundle(release=None)) (plan names this release's own spec ids) gives, ORIGINAL, one correct ground `{'release':'current'}, probe None, 'the plan names this release's own spec ids ... there is no earlier release whose capability to compare'` over all 8 contracts; MUTANT fabricates 5 grounds `{'release':'R', ...}` 'the probe is at capability N, the release's ... version did not move' — a false claim that the approvals were carried across a comparison with R (ARCHITECTURE-EXCEPTION-V2-007 identity rule). `origin` feeds report['approvals_kept_grounds'][].from.release/.ground, report['semantic_changes'][].from.release and report['mapping'][].from_release (migrate bundle_cli.py:397,407,438). RAN the registered kill file tests.v2.test_v21_migrate_semantics against the mutant: SURVIVED (51 OK) — because at this snapshot RELEASES has one entry ('2.0.0') and every 2.0.0 probe digest differs from current, so on LedgerLock and every fixture `old != s.id` and the overwrite never fires (verified: migrate(LedgerLock) report byte-identical orig vs mutant). The existing test test_a_bundle_already_of_this_release_loses_nothing (test_v21_migrate_semantics.py:489-497) already pins `[ground]=report['approvals_kept_grounds']` == a single {'release':'current'} group, but only under real RELEASES where the overwrite cannot arise. Not EQUIVALENT (observable, demonstrated); REFUTED because the owner (and the function's own docstring) depend on correct attribution and no test exercises the condition.

entries.refutation: A test is owed. Input: `with mock.patch.dict(bundle_cli.RELEASES, {'R': {'compiler_digest': bundle_cli.COMPILER_DIGEST, 'probes': {k:(e.probe_id,e.probe_digest,e.capability_version) for k,e in catalog.active().items()}}}): out, report = bundle_cli.migrate(era_bundle(release=None))`. Reader: report['approvals_kept_grounds']. Assert it is a single group with from=={'release':'current'}, probe is None, 'no earlier release whose capability to compare', covering all contracts (i.e. a spec whose `old` equals its current id keeps 'current' attribution, not 'R'). Under the `or` mutant this becomes >=2 'release R' grounds and `[ground] = report['approvals_kept_grounds']` raises ValueError. Complementary case for the docstring invariant: two RELEASES entries R1 (earlier) and R2 both compiling a given spec to the same old id, a bundle whose plan names that old id; assert report['mapping'][old]['from_release'] == 'R1' (first attribution); the mutant gives 'R2'.

entries.group: T03a-order-of-an-id-list: `sorted(kept)` -> `list(kept)` only reorders rows of report['approvals_kept_grounds'] and the ids within each row; the set of groups, their membership and their ground text are unchanged (cf. carried lint[4][5], except kept is a set so list() is non-deterministic).
entries.grounds: bundle_cli.py:306 `keys = {name: _group(...) for name in sorted(kept)}` -> `for name in list(kept)`. `kept` is a set[str] (bundle_cli.py:432 `{ap['contract_id'] for ap in candidate['approvals']}`), so `list(kept)` is hash-randomised (non-deterministic across processes). Effect: the insertion order of `keys` changes, which changes (i) the row order of the returned list (`dict.fromkeys(keys.values())`) and (ii) the order of ids in each row's `contracts` list; the representative chosen by `next(n for n in keys if keys[n]==key)` also changes, but all members of a group share probe/class/subject_absence/release/versions (the group key) and hence the same `consulted` and ground text, so `_ground` is identical regardless of representative. MEASURED on migrate(LedgerLock): orig vs mutant give the same 8 groups with identical membership and ground text (group-set-as-frozensets equal: True; whole report equal after canonicalising grounds order: True); only the row order and within-row id order differ, and 3 in-process runs reproduced a stable-but-reordered output. RAN the registered kill file tests.v2.test_v21_migrate_semantics against the mutant: SURVIVED (51 OK). Observable (so not EQUIVALENT), but no consumer depends on the order; AUDITED.
